good_tf:
resource "azurerm_network_security_rule" "example" {
  name                        = "allow-http"
  priority                    = 100
  direction                   = "Inbound"
  access                      = "Allow"
  protocol                    = "Tcp"
  source_port_range           = "*"
  destination_port_range      = "80"
  source_address_prefix       = "10.0.0.0/16" # FIX: restrict HTTP access to internal network
  destination_address_prefix  = "*"
  resource_group_name         = "example-rg"
  network_security_group_name = "example-nsg"
}
why_it_matters: Unencrypted HTTP traffic on port 80 exposes web app data to interception and tampering by any adversary on the internet path.
Allowing wildcards in source address prefixes permits arbitrary public IP addresses to initiate cleartext TCP connections directly to network interfaces.
Restricting source prefixes to explicit internal subnets or blocking public port 80 forces traffic through TLS-terminating reverse proxies or private endpoints.
post_en:
Network security rules allowing inbound TCP port 80 from wildcard source addresses expose backend web instances to unencrypted internet traffic.
Set source_address_prefix to a specific internal IP block like 10.0.0.0/16 instead of a wildcard or Internet.
This restricts direct unencrypted HTTP ingress to trusted network segments and prevents opportunistic external scanning.
CKV_AZURE_160 fails the first version and passes the second.
